title: NEVER Pay Steakhouse Prices Again — This Old Butcher Trick Turns a $5 Chuck Roast Into Ribeye
description:
🥩 Subscribe for an old Boston butcher's trick every week — the whole chuck eye method, every measure and the arithmetic, is written out below 👇

A young mailman came into my shop holding a receipt: two ribeyes downtown for his anniversary, $164 before the tip. Inside a $5-a-pound chuck roast there's a steak that eats like a ribeye, because it's the same muscle. Here's where it is, how to cut it out and how to cook it so nobody at your table can tell. From 54 years behind the counter of my shop in Dorchester, Boston.

⭐ 7 OLD BUTCHER TRICKS
1. Pick the roast from the RIB END. Turn the package over: you want one round eye of meat about the size of your fist, a thin ring of fat and fine white flecks all through it. That's the chuck eye. Only thick white seams and no eye = neck end, that one's for the stew pot. Ask for "the first cut", 2-3 lb, at least 3 inches tall.
2. Follow the seams with your knife. Eye side up, slide the tip into the thin white lines between the muscles and pull the muscle away. Keep the trimmings for stew or burgers. Trim the hard silver skin, leave the soft fat (soft gives, silver fights back).
3. Cut it thick and across the grain: 1½ inches at least. A thin steak goes gray all the way through before it browns. 20 minutes in the freezer (firm, not frozen) for even steaks. You get 3-4 steaks from a 3 lb roast.
4. Salt it the night before: about ¾ tsp coarse kosher salt per pound, both sides and the edges, on a wire rack over a plate, in the fridge UNCOVERED. Overnight or 24 h. No time? At least 45 minutes ahead, never 10.
5. Cook it cold: straight from the refrigerator, pat it dry with a paper towel. An hour on the counter only warms the middle 2-3 degrees and makes the outside wet again.
6. A screaming hot pan: cast iron or heavy steel, no nonstick. Medium-high, 5 minutes empty, 1 tbsp oil until the first wisp of smoke. Flip it every minute. Stand it on its edge 30 seconds to render the fat. Last 2 minutes: 2 tbsp butter, 2 crushed garlic cloves, a sprig of thyme or rosemary, tilt and spoon it over.
7. Pull it at 130°F (not 125, the chuck eye has more fat to melt), rest 5 minutes on a warm plate with the pan butter over it, then slice thin, across the grain, knife at a slant. A pinch of flaky salt.

🛠 IF IT GOES WRONG
Chewy = you cut along the grain. Tough and full of gristle = a neck-end roast with no eye. Gray with no crust = the pan wasn't hot or the steak was wet. Too well done = too thin: 1½ inches and trust the thermometer, not the clock. Smoke alarm went off = you did it right.

💵 THE ARITHMETIC
Steakhouse: $164 for two steaks before the tip. Ribeye at the meat counter: about $16/lb, $32 for two at home. Chuck roast: 3 lb × $5 = $15, plus about $2 of butter, garlic and thyme. $17, steak for four, and a pound of trimmings for another supper.
